### About Me

I was born into a working-class family and grew up in a free, supportive environment. Since 2017, I have pursued environmental soil microbiology with a focus on microbial processes regulating greenhouse gas fluxes across diverse ecosystems. My research integrates microbial cultivation, genome-resolved metagenomics, and genome-scale metabolic modeling to investigate novel microbial N<sub>2</sub>O sinks.

I am currently a postdoctoral research associate in the [Löffler Lab](https://loefflerlab.utk.edu), where I study the physiology and genomics of N<sub>2</sub>O-reducing bacteria, with implications for climate-smart agriculture and biogeochemical cycling. <br>

<strong><u>I am always open to collaborative opportunities and welcome connections with researchers interested in microbial physiology, environmental microbiology, and greenhouse gas mitigation.</u></strong>

### Research Focus

-   Microbial N<sub>2</sub>O sinks in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems\
-   Cultivation of fastidious microorganisms\
-   Denitrification and respiratory versatility in soil bacteria\
-   Synthetic microbiomes for bioaugmentation in regenerative agriculture
